title: Judges Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 20.

questions.question: Where did all the children of Israel gather together as one man?
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpeh
questions.explanation: Judges 20:1 states that the congregation was gathered together as one man unto the LORD in Mizpeh.

questions.question: How many footmen that drew sword did the chiefs of all the tribes of Israel present themselves with?
questions.correctAnswer: Four hundred thousand
questions.explanation: Judges 20:2 says that four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Mizpeh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 20:3 confirms that the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Mizpeh.

questions.question: Who answered the children of Israel about the wickedness done in Gibeah?
options: The Levite, husband of the woman slain
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite, husband of the woman slain
questions.explanation: Judges 20:4 says the Levite, husband of the woman that was slain, answered and told what happened in Gibeah.

questions.question: What did the men of Gibeah do to the Levite's concubine?
options: They forced her and she died
questions.correctAnswer: They forced her and she died
questions.explanation: Judges 20:5 explains that the men of Gibeah forced the Levite's concubine, and she died as a result.

questions.question: True or False: The Levite cut his concubine into pieces and sent her throughout all the inheritance of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 20:6 states the Levite cut his concubine into pieces and sent her throughout all the inheritance of Israel because of the wickedness committed.

questions.question: What was the response of all the people after hearing the Levite's words?
options: They arose as one man and vowed not to return to their tents
They sent a delegation to Gibeah
questions.correctAnswer: They arose as one man and vowed not to return to their tents
questions.explanation: Judges 20:8 records that all the people arose as one man and said none would go to his tent nor return to his house.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites decided to go up by lot against Gibeah to punish it.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 20:9 indicates that the Israelites resolved to go up by lot against Gibeah.

questions.question: What fraction of men from each tribe did Israel plan to take to fetch victual for the people?
options: One hundred men of a thousand
One thousand men of ten thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Ten men of an hundred
questions.explanation: Judges 20:10 details that Israel would take ten men of an hundred throughout the tribes to fetch victual for the people.

questions.question: How many men of Benjamin that drew sword were numbered at that time, excluding the inhabitants of Gibeah?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty and six thousand
questions.explanation: Judges 20:15 states that Benjamin had twenty and six thousand men that drew sword out of the cities.

questions.question: True or False: Among the men of Israel, there were seven hundred chosen men who were lefthanded and could sling stones very accurately.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 20:16 describes seven hundred chosen men lefthanded, each able to sling stones at a hair breadth and not miss.

questions.question: Who was to go up first to battle against the children of Benjamin, according to the LORD's counsel?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: Judges 20:18 records that the LORD said Judah shall go up first to battle.

questions.question: What did the tribes of Israel request from the tribe of Benjamin before the battle?
options: Deliver the wicked men in Gibeah to be put to death
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver the wicked men in Gibeah to be put to death
questions.explanation: Judges 20:13 shows Israel asked Benjamin to deliver the children of Belial in Gibeah for death to put away evil.

questions.question: What was the number of chosen men in Gibeah who sided with Benjamin?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven hundred
questions.explanation: Judges 20:15 specifies that beside the twenty-six thousand, there were seven hundred chosen men in Gibeah.

questions.question: In Judges 20, which event happened first?
options: The Levite cut his concubine into pieces
The children of Israel gathered as one man
The children of Benjamin gathered for battle
The men of Israel asked counsel of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel gathered as one man
questions.explanation: Judges 20:1 shows that all the children of Israel went out and gathered as one man before the other events occurred.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Judges 20:17, how many men of Israel, excluding Benjamin, were ready for battle?
questions.explanation: Judges 20:17 states that the men of Israel, excluding Benjamin, were numbered at four hundred thousand men that drew sword, all men of war.

questions.question: What guidance did the LORD give regarding which tribe should go first into battle against Benjamin, as recorded in Judges 20:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: In Judges 20:18, the LORD told the children of Israel that Judah should go up first to battle against the children of Benjamin after they sought counsel at the house of God.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites encamped against Gibeah in the evening according to Judges 20:19.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 20:19 indicates that the children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah, not in the evening.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the first day of battle between Israel and Benjamin as recorded in Judges 20:21?
options: Benjamin was defeated with heavy losses
Israel destroyed twenty-two thousand men of Benjamin
Benjamin destroyed twenty-two thousand men of Israel
The battle ended in a draw
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin destroyed twenty-two thousand men of Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 20:21 states that the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed twenty-two thousand men of Israel that day.

questions.question: How did the men of Israel respond after the first day's defeat according to Judges 20:22?
options: They encouraged themselves and set battle again in array
They prayed and waited for a sign
questions.correctAnswer: They encouraged themselves and set battle again in array
questions.explanation: Judges 20:22 tells us that after the defeat, the men of Israel encouraged themselves and arranged themselves again for battle in the same place as before.

questions.question: What does Judges 20:23 teach about the importance of prayer and seeking God's counsel in difficult situations?
options: Prayer is unnecessary if you have many warriors
The people wept and sought God's counsel before battle, showing dependence on Him
God's counsel is clear without seeking
questions.correctAnswer: The people wept and sought God's counsel before battle, showing dependence on Him
questions.explanation: Judges 20:23 shows that the children of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until evening and asked His counsel about going again to battle, demonstrating humility and trust in God.

questions.question: How did the LORD respond when Israel asked if they should go again to battle against Benjamin, according to Judges 20:23-24?
options: The LORD said to cease fighting
The LORD said to go up against Benjamin
The LORD said to seek another way
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD said to go up against Benjamin
questions.explanation: In Judges 20:23 and 20:24, the LORD instructed Israel to go up again against the children of Benjamin after they sought His counsel in prayer.

questions.question: True or False: On the second day, Benjamin destroyed eighteen thousand men of Israel, as stated in Judges 20:25.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 20:25 records that Benjamin went forth out of Gibeah the second day and destroyed eighteen thousand men of Israel, all of whom drew the sword.

questions.question: After the second day's battle, what acts of humility and dependence on God did the children of Israel perform as described in Judges 20:26?
options: They fasted, wept, sat before the LORD, and offered burnt and peace offerings
They took a vow of silence
questions.correctAnswer: They fasted, wept, sat before the LORD, and offered burnt and peace offerings
questions.explanation: Judges 20:26 shows the children of Israel fasting, weeping, sitting before the LORD, and offering burnt and peace offerings, demonstrating repentance and reliance on God.

questions.question: What assurance did the LORD give through Phinehas in Judges 20:28 about the third day of battle?
options: The battle would end in a draw
Israel would be delivered into Benjamin's hand
The LORD would deliver Benjamin into Israel's hand
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD would deliver Benjamin into Israel's hand
questions.explanation: Judges 20:28 records that the LORD said to go up to battle again because the next day He would deliver Benjamin into Israel's hand.

questions.question: What tactical strategy did Israel use around Gibeah on the third day according to Judges 20:29-30?
options: Set liers in wait around the city and put themselves in array as before
questions.correctAnswer: Set liers in wait around the city and put themselves in array as before
questions.explanation: Judges 20:29-30 describe that Israel set liers in wait around Gibeah and arranged their army as before to deceive and trap Benjamin.

questions.question: How does Judges 20:31-32 illustrate the use of deception in battle?
options: Benjamin was drawn away from the city, thinking they were winning, but Israel planned to draw them further away
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin was drawn away from the city, thinking they were winning, but Israel planned to draw them further away
questions.explanation: In Judges 20:31-32, Benjamin was drawn away from the city after killing about thirty men, thinking they had the advantage, while Israel planned to flee and draw them to the highways for an ambush.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trusting God's timing and strategy can be learned from the events of Judges 20:17-32?
options: Victory depends solely on numbers and strength
Seeking God's counsel and trusting His timing leads to ultimate victory despite initial setbacks
Human wisdom is sufficient without God
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking God's counsel and trusting His timing leads to ultimate victory despite initial setbacks
questions.explanation: The passage from Judges 20:17-32 shows that although Israel suffered losses initially, their persistence in seeking God's counsel and obeying His instructions led to eventual victory, illustrating faith and trust in God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 20:27, the ark of the covenant was present when Israel inquired of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 20:27 specifically mentions that the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days when Israel enquired of the LORD.

questions.question: How does Judges 20:18-19 emphasize the importance of obedience following God's direction?
options: Israel ignored God's command and acted on their own
Israel immediately obeyed by rising early and encamping against Gibeah after God's direction
Israel delayed in obeying God's command
questions.correctAnswer: Israel immediately obeyed by rising early and encamping against Gibeah after God's direction
questions.explanation: Judges 20:18-19 shows that after the LORD directed Judah to go first into battle, the children of Israel rose early and encamped against Gibeah, highlighting quick obedience to God's guidance.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 20.

questions.question: What was the appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait during the battle at Gibeah?
options: A great flame with smoke rising from the city
A white banner raised on the city wall
questions.correctAnswer: A great flame with smoke rising from the city
questions.explanation: Judges 20:38 states that the appointed sign was to make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city, signaling coordination between Israel’s forces and the liers in wait.

questions.question: In Judges 20, what was the strategy used by the men of Israel to trap the Benjamites during the third day of battle?
options: They set fire to the fields surrounding Gibeah
They feigned retreat to draw Benjamin out of the city
They attacked from the rear while Benjamin was engaged
They poisoned the wells around Gibeah
questions.correctAnswer: They feigned retreat to draw Benjamin out of the city
questions.explanation: Judges 20:32 describes how Israel’s men decided to flee to lure Benjamin from Gibeah to the highways, enabling an ambush. This tactic was a key part of their battle plan.

questions.question: How many men of valour from Benjamin fell in the battle as recorded in Judges 20?
questions.explanation: Judges 20:46 records that twenty and five thousand men of valour from Benjamin fell that day, indicating the scale and severity of the battle.

questions.question: Where did the six hundred men of Benjamin flee to and remain for four months?
questions.correctAnswer: Rock Rimmon
questions.explanation: Judges 20:47 states that six hundred men fled to the wilderness to the rock Rimmon and stayed there four months, showing the last refuge of the Benjamites.

questions.question: According to Judges 20, who stood before the ark of the covenant when the Israelites sought counsel from the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Phinehas
questions.explanation: Judges 20:28 mentions that Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, stood before the ark when Israel enquired of the LORD, emphasizing his priestly role in this crisis.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning is significant in the description of the 700 chosen men who were left-handed in Judges 20:16?
options: Men cursed for their left hand
Men who could only fight with the left hand
questions.correctAnswer: Slingers with precise aim
questions.explanation: Judges 20:16 highlights that the seven hundred chosen men were left-handed and could sling stones at a hair's breadth without missing, showing exceptional skill rather than weakness. The word for 'lefthanded' here indicates a special military advantage.

questions.question: Which tribe did the LORD say should go up first to battle against the children of Benjamin?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: Judges 20:18 records that after seeking the LORD's counsel, the LORD said that Judah should lead the first attack, indicating divine direction in the battle.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 20, the children of Benjamin hearkened to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel and delivered the wicked men of Gibeah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 20:13 clearly states that the children of Benjamin refused to listen to their brethren and did not deliver the wicked men, prompting the war.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently displayed in Judges 20 through the repeated cycles of battle, seeking God’s counsel, and renewed fighting?
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition and cyclical motif
questions.explanation: Judges 20:21-28 shows repeated cycles where Israel battles Benjamin, suffers losses, seeks God’s counsel, and then renews the fight. This cyclical repetition reinforces the theme of dependence on God’s guidance.

questions.question: How does the battle in Judges 20 foreshadow the New Testament theme of brotherly conflict and reconciliation?
options: It shows the consequences of sin among God’s people
It portrays the need for a mediator between conflicted brothers
It reflects the brokenness that Jesus came to heal
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: The violent conflict between Israel and Benjamin in Judges 20 highlights sin’s destructive effects and the need for mediation and reconciliation, themes echoed in the New Testament (e.g., Matthew 5:23-24 and 2 Corinthians 5:18).

questions.question: Which other biblical passage connects closely with Judges 20 in its theme of civil conflict and the need for justice within Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 11
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11 describes a conflict involving the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of Israel, connecting with Judges 20’s theme of civil strife and the quest for justice within the nation.

questions.question: According to Judges 20, what was the outcome of the battle for the cities and the beasts belonging to the children of Benjamin?
options: They were destroyed and set on fire
They were given to other tribes
questions.correctAnswer: They were destroyed and set on fire
questions.explanation: Judges 20:48 indicates that Israel destroyed the men, beasts, and cities of Benjamin and set the cities on fire, highlighting the totality of the judgment.

questions.question: What role does the ark of the covenant play in Judges 20 during the Israelites’ inquiry of the LORD?
options: It was carried into battle as a standard
It was present as a symbol of God’s presence during prayer
It was hidden to prevent capture
It was used to curse the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: It was present as a symbol of God’s presence during prayer
questions.explanation: Judges 20:27 states that the ark of the covenant was there during the inquiry, symbolizing God’s presence and authority as Israel sought His will in their crisis.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Israel were initially successful in battle against Benjamin and won the first day without any losses.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 20:21 reveals that Benjamin killed twenty-two thousand men of Israel on the first day, showing that Israel suffered heavy losses initially.

questions.question: Why did the men of Israel fast and weep before the LORD after their second day of battle against Benjamin?
options: Because they had not yet won and sought God’s favor
Because they wanted to mourn the Benjamites
Because they were celebrating a victory
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had not yet won and sought God’s favor
questions.explanation: Judges 20:26 describes Israel fasting and weeping before the LORD after suffering heavy losses, indicating their dependence on God’s guidance for victory.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Judges 20:28 reveal about God's guidance in times of national crisis?
options: God promises deliverance to His people
God delegates decisions to human leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God promises deliverance to His people
questions.explanation: Judges 20:28 shows that the LORD promised deliverance by saying, 'for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand,' indicating God's active providence and assurance in conflict.

questions.question: How does the account in Judges 20:6 illustrate the gravity of sin within Israel?
options: Sin leads to God's immediate punishment on the nation
Sin causes internal disunity and judgment
Sin is easily forgiven without consequences
Sin is ignored by the community
questions.correctAnswer: Sin causes internal disunity and judgment
questions.explanation: In Judges 20:6, the Levite cut his concubine into pieces and sent her throughout Israel because of the lewdness and folly committed, illustrating how sin brought severe internal judgment and division among God's people.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by the unity of Israel's tribes in gathering against Benjamin as described in Judges 20:1-2?
options: The doctrine of the church's unity in Christ
The doctrine of God's sovereignty over nations
The doctrine of corporate responsibility and justice
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of corporate responsibility and justice
questions.explanation: Judges 20:1-2 describe all Israel gathering as one man to address wickedness, showing the corporate responsibility for upholding justice within God's covenant community.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Judges 20:18 when Israel sought His counsel before battle?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omniscience
questions.explanation: Judges 20:18 shows Israel asking God which tribe should go first, and God answers, revealing His all-knowing nature in directing His people’s actions.

questions.question: How does Judges 20:16 reflect on divine providence in human abilities within the community?
options: God endowed specific skills for His purposes
Human skill is independent of God
Skills are irrelevant in God's plans
questions.correctAnswer: God endowed specific skills for His purposes
questions.explanation: Verse 16 notes 700 chosen left-handed men skilled in slinging stones, suggesting God’s providential gifting of abilities to fulfill his purposes in Israel’s defense.

questions.question: What theological truth emerges from comparing Judges 20:23 and 20:28 about Israel’s worship and battle?
options: God answers prayer and directs battle outcomes
Israel acted independently of God’s will
Battles are won solely by numbers
questions.correctAnswer: God answers prayer and directs battle outcomes
questions.explanation: Verses 23 and 28 show Israel weeping, seeking counsel, and receiving direct guidance from God, demonstrating the necessity of divine direction in human conflict.

questions.question: According to Judges 20:47-48, what does Israel’s final destruction of Benjamin’s cities reveal about God’s justice?
options: God’s justice is delayed but certain
God’s justice is limited to individuals
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice is delayed but certain
questions.explanation: The final burning of the cities in verses 47-48 shows that God’s judgment upon sin is thorough and inevitable, even if it requires time and repeated efforts.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about sin and repentance can be drawn from Judges 20:26 and 20:23?
options: True repentance involves fasting, weeping, and seeking God’s will
God does not respond to communal repentance
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance involves fasting, weeping, and seeking God’s will
questions.explanation: Both verses describe Israel fasting, weeping, and offering sacrifices before God, highlighting the biblical doctrine that genuine repentance includes heartfelt mourning and seeking divine guidance.

questions.question: How does Judges 20:13 illustrate the doctrine of free will within corporate sin?
options: Benjamin freely chose to protect the wicked men
Benjamin was forced into sin by other tribes
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin freely chose to protect the wicked men
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows Benjamin refused to hand over the guilty men, demonstrating human free will in choosing sin and resisting communal calls for justice.

questions.question: What does Judges 20:35 teach about God's sovereignty in battle outcomes?
options: Victory depends solely on Israel’s strength
The LORD actively strikes down enemies in battle
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD actively strikes down enemies in battle
questions.explanation: Verse 35 explicitly states 'the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel,' affirming God’s sovereign role in determining victory in battle.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of Judges 20 teach about the consequences of Israel’s moral failure?
options: Sin leads to national violence and near destruction
Moral failure leads only to personal consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to national violence and near destruction
questions.explanation: The chapter shows how sin in Gibeah led to civil war and massive loss, illustrating the biblical theme that communal sin brings devastating consequences (Judges 20:6, 44).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s command for Israel to attack Benjamin in Judges 20 is immoral. What does Judges 20:26-28 teach about the character and justice of God in this scenario?
options: God acts justly after Israel’s repentance and seeks to remove evil
God supports violence without moral reason
God has no involvement in human justice
questions.correctAnswer: God acts justly after Israel’s repentance and seeks to remove evil
questions.explanation: Verses 26-28 show Israel’s mourning, fasting, and seeking God’s counsel before battle, indicating God’s judgment is righteous and follows a process of repentance and justice removal, not arbitrary violence.

questions.question: What does Judges 20:42-43 reveal about God’s justice and mercy in the battle’s aftermath?
options: God allows some to escape as a remnant
questions.correctAnswer: God allows some to escape as a remnant
questions.explanation: Verses 42-43 describe some Benjamites fleeing and being pursued, but 600 men escaped and hid, showing God’s justice with mercy by preserving a remnant.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is displayed in Judges 20:1 when Israel assembled 'as one man' to seek the LORD at Mizpeh?
options: God’s unifying presence among His people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s unifying presence among His people
questions.explanation: The united assembly in verse 1 indicates God’s presence as the central point of Israel’s unity, reflecting His attribute of being a unifier of His covenant people.

questions.question: How does Judges 20:31-34 demonstrate the strategic wisdom God imparts to His people in warfare?
options: God’s people use deception and ambush strategically
God forbids any form of military tactics
Victory depends only on brute force
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people use deception and ambush strategically
questions.explanation: These verses describe Israel’s tactical use of liers in wait and drawing out Benjamin from the city, demonstrating God-guided military wisdom.
